title: Blanquette de Veau
description: Blanquette de veau (veal stew) is sometimes called the Mother of all French dishes. It’s the ultimate French home cooked meal, so traditional, bourgeois yet simple. In Julia Child's “Mastering the Art of French Cooking,” she emphasized to students that it's important not to brown anything in the dish. The end result should be completely white, with some parsley flakes.
ingredients: 6 sprigs flat-leaf parsley, plus 2 tablespoons, chopped
directions: In a 4-quart casserole place stock, veal, onion, celery, leeks, garlic, cloves, 1 cup mushrooms, thyme and parsley sprigs, bay leaf, and salt and pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer for 1 1/2 hours, skimming frequently.
Boil pearl onions with a little water in a skillet for about 5 minutes, until almost dry. Add some oil and the remaining mushrooms and cook gently until tender. Set aside.
When veal is tender, drain the pot, reserving 3 cups stock, and discarding the vegetables and herbs.

Wipe out casserole and melt butter in it. Whisk in flour, cook one minute. Whisk in stock, cook 5 minutes. Whisk in cream. Add veal, mushrooms, and onions. Simmer 5 minutes and re-season (salt, pepper, maybe some lemon juice).
Serve, garnished with chopped parsley, maybe with rice or noodles, and a green vegetable or roasted carrots.
